knowledge_answers.rationale: A struck ball that first grounds inside before crossing normally earns four, not six.
A catch is not complete until control of ball and movement is achieved; grounding on the boundary while still carrying the ball beforehand makes the ball grounded beyond the boundary.
Obstructing the field generally requires wilful obstruction or distraction; accidental obstruction is expressly not out.

The wicket state is assessed before the new action; where one bail is already off, removing the remaining bail is sufficient; holding the ball while doing so is a fair method of putting down the wicket.

An authorised substitute acts as a fielder for this purpose; no illegal fielding or boundary grounding invalidates the act; control of ball and movement before ground contact completes a fair catch and dismisses the striker.
